sourceGaps: The obtained source is The Competition Problems from the International Chemistry Olympiads, Volume 3, edited by Anton Sirota, IUVENTA/IChO International Information Centre, Bratislava 2014. This is its collection edition of the 43rd IChO, 9–18 July 2011, Ankara, Turkey, not an obtained complete original competitor packet. Original grading points, selected practical grading graphs and data-dependent solution portions are omitted by the collection editors. Every instruction, procedure, chemical list, native key, rubric, diagram and form actually printed in physical pages111–162 is retained.

Separate practical answer sheets, the ammonia-borane blank recording table and Graphs2.1/2.2 are referenced but not supplied in the obtained section or complete four-PDF archive folder. Competitor measurements, missing blank forms and original score allocations are not invented.

Practical1 and Practical3 refer to jury-approved distribution/evaluation graphs which are not printed. Practical2 supplies a ten-row reference-volume table and graph but no worked numerical answers for2.4–2.6. Practical3 supplies native grading conditions and Rf ranges but no competitor yields. All printed content is retained, without invented omitted graphs, calculations, measurements or marking points.

The printed Volume3 rights notice permits teaching copying, distribution, transmission and adaptation with its required Volume3 reference; commercial publication/distribution requires a waiver from the copyright holder. Mandatory attribution and the 2014 collection edition are retained, without claiming organizer hosting, unrestricted commercial use or completeness of the original2011 packet.

Only new physical pages111–165 were personally read in this pass. Historical common1–5 source reading is reused with zero fresh credit. The complete2011 annual section ends162. Pages163–165 begin the44th2012 section and a connected theoretical Problem1 continuing beyond165; these three pages are boundary evidence only, excluded from both2011 candidates. Physical166–291 remains unread/unclaimed and the parent compilation unresolved.

sourceErrors.finding: The conversion of epsilon_HD to its per-mole value prints45 600 kJ mol−1, while the following deltaH is0.6544 kJ mol−1. The printed intermediate unit/result is retained and qualified.

Key3.2 prints frequency1.1428·10−14 s. Key3.4 prints6.6261·10−34 as the numerator of the eV conversion and prints minus(31.675) in its generic dissociation-energy expression. All three literal discrepancies are preserved with attribution.
The forbidden(2,2) case is followed by a copied kinetic-energy expression16.1−14.677=1.4eV despite the preceding24.880eV threshold. The native expression and conclusion are retained and qualified.
Key4.2 prose prints0.04mol hydrogen, while its time calculation uses0.40mol; both printed values are retained.
Key5.2 heading prints cyclicN5+ although the question and five drawn resonance structures refer to the anionN5−. Heading and negative diagrams are retained.

Key5.7 first metathesis equation prints anAsF6 reactant andCsSbF6 product; its second equation prints2KSbF6 despite singleN5SbF6/K reagent coefficients. The exact printed equations are preserved and qualified.

Limited own native equation reopen confirms3.5 prints a second minus sign inIP(H)=−13.5984/∞²−13.5984/1²=13.598eV. The literal sign/result are preserved and qualified, with no new full-source reading claim.
